result.summary: Deprecates named watch-only wallet RPC arguments that are already treated as no-ops. This initiates the standard Bitcoin Core deprecation cycle for these options ahead of their eventual removal.
result.problem: Certain watch-only wallet RPC options were previously made no-ops but remain present in the RPC interface without formal deprecation enforcement or warnings, leaving dead parameters in client-facing APIs.
evidence: PR description: "Since 'leet' commit 1337c72198a7d32935431d64e9e58c12f9003abc, the options are deprecated no-ops, so it seems time to properly start a deprecation cycle for them."
result.scope_notes: The diff and file list are omitted from the PR data, but the changes span 7 files with +45/-4 lines.
result.card: This PR formally deprecates named watch-only wallet RPC options that have already been converted to no-ops. It begins the standard deprecation cycle so that callers still passing these arguments receive deprecation warnings before the options are permanently removed. The author states the options have been no-ops since commit 1337c72198a7d32935431d64e9e58c12f9003abc.
uncertainties: The specific RPC methods and named options being deprecated cannot be verified without the diff or file list.

risk.why: Mistakes in RPC parameter parsing or deprecation handling could break existing RPC client scripts that provide these arguments.
